claim: Affinity matured self-reactive antibodies are found in autoimmune diseases like systemic lupus erythematous.
source: Affinity matured self-reactive antibodies are found in autoimmune diseases like systemic lupus erythematous.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about autoimmune diseases, specifically SLE.

claim: Antibody-secreting cells (ASCs) from spontaneous GCs grouped into multiple subclusters.
source: Antibody-secreting cells (ASCs) and memory B cells (MemBs) from spontaneous GCs grouped into multiple subclusters.
evidence: This claim is supported by the single-cell transcriptomics analysis presented in the study.

claim: Memory B cells (MemBs) from spontaneous GCs grouped into multiple subclusters.
source: Antibody-secreting cells (ASCs) and memory B cells (MemBs) from spontaneous GCs grouped into multiple subclusters.
evidence: This claim is supported by the single-cell transcriptomics analysis presented in the study.

claim: ASCs matured into two terminal clusters with distinct secretion profiles.

claim: ASCs matured into two terminal clusters with distinct antibody repertoire profiles.
source: ASCs matured into two terminal clusters, with distinct secretion, antibody repertoire and metabolic profiles.
evidence: This is supported by VDJ sequencing showing differences in isotype usage and mutation accumulation.

claim: ASCs matured into two terminal clusters with distinct metabolic profiles.
source: ASCs matured into two terminal clusters, with distinct secretion, antibody repertoire and metabolic profiles.

claim: MemBs contained FCRL5+ subsets.

claim: MemBs contained CD23+ subsets.

claim: FCRL5+ and CD23+ MemB subsets have different in vivo localization in the spleen.
source: MemBs contained FCRL5+ and CD23+ subsets, with different in vivo localization in the spleen.

claim: GC-derived FCRL5+ MemBs share transcriptomic properties with atypical B cells found in aging and infection.
source: GC-derived FCRL5+ MemBs share transcriptomic and repertoire properties with atypical B cells found in aging and infection and localize to the marginal zone, suggesting a similar contribution to recall responses.
evidence: This is based on comparison of gene expression markers with published literature on atypical memory B cells.

claim: GC-derived FCRL5+ MemBs share repertoire properties with atypical B cells found in aging and infection.
source: GC-derived FCRL5+ MemBs share transcriptomic and repertoire properties with atypical B cells found in aging and infection and localize to the marginal zone, suggesting a similar contribution to recall responses.

claim: GC-derived FCRL5+ MemBs localize to the marginal zone.
source: GC-derived FCRL5+ MemBs share transcriptomic and repertoire properties with atypical B cells found in aging and infection and localize to the marginal zone, suggesting a similar contribution to recall responses.
evidence: This is supported by confocal microscopy and in vivo CD45 labeling experiments.

claim: GC-derived FCRL5+ MemBs may contribute to recall responses similarly to atypical B cells.
source: GC-derived FCRL5+ MemBs share transcriptomic and repertoire properties with atypical B cells found in aging and infection and localize to the marginal zone, suggesting a similar contribution to recall responses.
evidence: This is a speculative inference based on the observed similarities and localization.

claim: ASC and MemB subsets maintained an underlying clonal redundancy despite being transcriptomically diverse.
source: While transcriptomically diverse, ASC and MemB subsets maintained an underlying clonal redundancy.
evidence: This is supported by clonal intersection analysis showing shared clones across different subclusters.

claim: Self-reactive clones could escape subset-targeting therapy by perpetuation of self-reactivity in distinct subsets.
source: Therefore, self-reactive clones could escape subset-targeting therapy by perpetuation of self-reactivity in distinct subsets.
evidence: This is an inference based on the observed clonal redundancy across subsets.

claim: In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), pathogenesis is caused by self-reactive antibody-secreting cells (ASCs).
source: In autoimmune diseases like systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), pathogenesis is caused by self-reactive antibody-secreting cells (ASCs) and sustained by memory B cells (MemBs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SLE pathogenesis.

claim: In systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), pathogenesis is sustained by memory B cells (MemBs).
source: In autoimmune diseases like systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE), pathogenesis is caused by self-reactive antibody-secreting cells (ASCs) and sustained by memory B cells (MemBs).
evidence: This is established knowledge about SLE pathogenesis.

claim: The major known subsets of MemBs are conventional germinal center (GC)- and non-GC-derived MemBs.
source: Among MemBs, the major known subsets are conventional germinal center (GC)- and non-GC-derived MemBs (Taylor et al., 2012; Viant et al., 2021).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Atypical MemBs (AtMemBs) are present in models of acute and chronic infection in mice.
source: In addition, atypical MemBs (AtMemBs) are present in models of acute and chronic infection in mice (Kim et al., 2019; Song et al., 2022), as well as in parasitic infection in humans (Portugal et al., 2017) and are similar to the age-associated B cells first described in ageing and autoimmune mouse models (Phalke and Marrack, 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Atypical MemBs (AtMemBs) are present in parasitic infection in humans.

evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Atypical MemBs are similar to age-associated B cells first described in ageing and autoimmune mouse models.

claim: DN2 (IgD−CD27−) cells resemble AtMemB cells and are an expanded subset of B cells in human SLE.
source: DN2 (IgD−CD27−) cells resemble AtMemB cells and are an expanded subset of B cells in human SLE.

claim: DN2 cells likely have a naive B cell origin.
source: They likely have a naive B cell origin, and data suggest they can be readily activated to mature into ASCs in the extrafollicular space (Jenks et al., 2018).

claim: DN2 cells can be readily activated to mature into ASCs in the extrafollicular space.
source: They likely have a naive B cell origin, and data suggest they can be readily activated to mature into ASCs in the extrafollicular space (Jenks et al., 2018).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: ASCs can segregate into different subsets with specific properties related to lifespan (short- and long-lived).
source: ASCs can also segregate into different subsets with specific properties related to lifespan (short- and long-lived) (Nutt et al., 2015; Radbruch et al., 2006) and origin (GC- and EF-derived) (Elsner and Shlomchik, 2020), though data on the differences in the metabolic profile and clonal overlap between these populations are still lacking.

claim: ASCs can segregate into different subsets with specific properties related to origin (GC- and EF-derived).
source: ASCs can also segregate into different subsets with specific properties related to lifespan (short- and long-lived) (Nutt et al., 2015; Radbruch et al., 2006) and origin (GC- and EF-derived) (Elsner and Shlomchik, 2020), though data on the differences in the metabolic profile and clonal overlap between these populations are still lacking.
evidence: This is supported by citations to previous literature.

claim: Experiments with LPS-driven derivation of B cells into ASCs have demonstrated the existence of multiple clusters of ASCs as they mature into alternate terminal states.
source: Importantly, experiments with LPS-driven derivation of B cells into ASCs have demonstrated the existence of multiple clusters of ASCs as they mature into alternate terminal states (Scharer et al., 2020).

claim: In SLE, isotype-class switching and somatic hypermutations of autoreactive antibodies indicate antibody maturation in GCs.
source: In SLE, isotype-class switching and somatic hypermutations of autoreactive antibodies indicate antibody maturation in GCs (Cappione et al., 2005).
evidence: This is supported by citation to previous literature.

claim: A total of 12,839 cells were retained post quality control for further analysis.
source: A total of 12,839 cells (9535 from 5 autoimmune chimeras, 3304 from 3 immunized chimeras) were retained post quality control for further analysis.
evidence: This is a direct statement of the data processing results.

claim: 9535 cells from 5 autoimmune chimeras were retained post quality control.
source: A total of 12,839 cells (9535 from 5 autoimmune chimeras, 3304 from 3 immunized chimeras) were retained post quality control for further analysis.

claim: 3304 cells from 3 immunized chimeras were retained post quality control.

claim: Expression of the EYFP reporter transcripts was confirmed.
source: Expression of the EYFP reporter transcripts was confirmed.
evidence: This is a statement about validation of the experimental system.

claim: Using unsupervised clustering, the cells grouped into four clusters.
source: Using unsupervised clustering, the cells grouped into four clusters (Figure 1B), representing the major known B cell compartments: GC B cells (e.g. S1pr2), which are either dark zone (DZ, e.g. Mki67) or light zone (LZ, e.g. Cd83), ASCs (e.g. Xbp1), and MemBs (e.g. Sell) (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by the UMAP visualization and marker gene expression shown in Figure 1B and 1C.

claim: The four clusters represent the major known B cell compartments: GC B cells (dark zone and light zone), ASCs, and MemBs.
source: Using unsupervised clustering, the cells grouped into four clusters (Figure 1B), representing the major known B cell compartments: GC B cells (e.g. S1pr2), which are either dark zone (DZ, e.g. Mki67) or light zone (LZ, e.g. Cd83), ASCs (e.g. Xbp1), and MemBs (e.g. Sell) (Figure 1C, Figure 1—figure supplement 1A).
evidence: This is supported by marker gene expression analysis shown in Figure 1C.

claim: All compartments (LZ, DZ, MemB, and ASC clusters) were clearly represented in both autoimmune and immunized conditions.
source: All compartments, LZ, DZ, MemB, and ASC clusters were clearly represented in both conditions (Figure 1D).
evidence: This is supported by the proportion analysis shown in Figure 1D.

claim: Clones with clear expansion were observed in both autoimmune and immunized chimeras.
source: Using paired single-cell BCR sequencing and repertoire analysis, we observed clones with clear expansion in both autoimmune and immunized chimeras (Figure 1—figure supplement 1B).
evidence: This is supported by the clonal proportion analysis shown in Figure 1—figure supplement 1B.

claim: In both conditions, clones were found that had members belonging to all four clusters.
source: Indeed, in both conditions, we were able to find clones that had members belonging to all four clusters, exemplified by the phylogenetics of the most expanded clone in one autoimmune chimeric mouse (Figure 1E).
evidence: This is supported by the phylogenetic tree shown in Figure 1E.

claim: The GC mutational level was in a similar range between autoimmune and immunized conditions.
source: The GC mutational level was in a similar range between conditions, although autoimmune chimeras had more DZ and LZ replacement mutations.
evidence: This is based on analysis of replacement mutations shown in Figure 1F.

claim: Autoimmune chimeras had more DZ and LZ replacement mutations than immunized chimeras.
source: The GC mutational level was in a similar range between conditions, although autoimmune chimeras had more DZ and LZ replacement mutations.

claim: MemBs in autoimmune and immunized chimeras had a similar number of nucleotide replacement mutations.
source: MemBs in autoimmune and immunized chimeras had a similar number of nucleotide replacement mutations.

claim: ASCs accumulated more mutations in immunized chimeras than in autoimmune chimeras.
source: However, ASCs accumulated more mutations in immunized chimeras (Figure 1F).

claim: ASCs in both conditions reached similar maximum levels of mutations (20 nt in autoimmune and 19 nt in immunized chimeras).
source: Nevertheless, ASCs in both conditions reached similar maximum levels of mutations (20 nt in autoimmune and 19 nt in immunized chimeras).
evidence: This is based on analysis of replacement mutations.

claim: Cells from autoimmune chimeras showed more isotype diversification in all compartments.
source: Cells from autoimmune chimeras showed more isotype diversification in all compartments (Figure 1G).

claim: Autoimmune chimeras preferred IGHVs 1–50, 1–75, and 8–8.

claim: IGHV 1–64 was used at a similar proportion in both autoimmune and immunized conditions.

evidence: This is based on V gene usage analysis shown in Figure 1H.

claim: Commonly used V genes in both conditions had clonal usage frequency in a similar range to that observed in B cells from naïve mice.
source: Notably, commonly used V genes in both conditions had clonal usage frequency in a similar range to that observed in B cells from naïve mice (Figure 1—figure supplement 1E; Rettig et al., 2018).

claim: In the 564Igi mixed BM chimeric autoimmune model, B cells with a WT BCR repertoire expand in spontaneous GCs.
source: Thus, using single-cell RNA-seq, we confirmed that in the 564Igi mixed BM chimeric autoimmune model, B cells with a WT BCR repertoire break tolerance, expand in spontaneous GCs and develop into MemBs and ASCs in a seemingly unrestricted manner, much like they do in response to foreign antigens.
evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: In the 564Igi mixed BM chimeric autoimmune model, B cells with a WT BCR repertoire develop into MemBs and ASCs in a seemingly unrestricted manner.

evidence: This is a summary conclusion based on the single-cell RNA-seq data.

claim: B cells with a WT BCR repertoire develop into MemBs and ASCs in the autoimmune model much like they do in response to foreign antigens.

claim: Cluster ASC_Early_1 bears the highest Cd19 and lowest Sdc1 expression.

claim: ASC_Late_2 cells had higher expression of Cd28 than ASC_Late_1.
